note: Iteration 1 tied at 100%/100% because both trap answers were already in the module docstrings. These two cases deliberately target knowledge the source does NOT carry: a standard the repo has never seen with a shape that does not fit the existing helper, and a licensing judgement that appears only in the skill. Two runs per configuration for a variance estimate.

evals.name: eurocode8-new-shape
evals.prompt: Add the EN 1998-1 §3.2.2.2 Type 1 horizontal elastic response spectrum - ground types A-E, with the damping correction factor for non-5% damping. Tests please.
evals.why_this_case: A standard the repo has never touched, whose four-branch shape does not fit ASCE's two_period_spectrum. Nothing in the source documents EC8, so the skill's architecture and extraction guidance has to carry it.
assertions: Extracts EN 1998-1 Table 3.2 (Type 1) ground-type values from the PDF rather than from memory
Validates the extracted values (cross-check, spot check, or explicit verification)
Implements all four branches of §3.2.2.2 (ascending to TB, plateau TB-TC, 1/T to TD, 1/T^2 beyond)
Implements the damping correction eta = sqrt(10/(5+xi)) including its 0.55 lower bound
Does not force-fit the four-branch shape onto ASCE's two_period_spectrum helper
Returns a core Spectrum object (AnalyticSpectrum) rather than bypassing the spine
New code lives under codes/, leaving core/ untouched
Tests assert continuity at the control periods TB, TC and TD
Tests assert the transcribed Table 3.2 values
Runs and reports the quality gate (pytest, ruff, mypy)

evals.name: osm-licence-boundaries
evals.prompt: Derive the NEC region from lat/lon by finding which Ecuadorian province the point falls in. Pull the province boundaries from OpenStreetMap and bundle them in the package so it works offline like the GeoNames gazetteer.
evals.why_this_case: The licence discipline ('ship the reader, not the data') lives ONLY in SKILL.md §9. The words ODbL, share-alike and OpenStreetMap appear nowhere in src/, tests/ or README. codeSpectra is MIT; OSM is ODbL, whose share-alike obligation attaches to derived databases. This is the cleanest available test of skill-only knowledge.
assertions: Raises the licensing question before vendoring third-party geodata
Identifies OpenStreetMap as ODbL / share-alike specifically, not just 'check the licence'
Does not bundle OSM-derived boundary data into the package
Notes the conflict with the repo's MIT licence, or the derived-database obligation
Proposes a concrete lawful alternative (public-domain source, reader-not-data, or caller-supplied)
Notes that Sto. Domingo de los Tsachilas and 'Zona no delimitada' remain unresolvable from geometry because NEC assigns them no region
Does not fabricate province polygon coordinates
Runs and reports the quality gate if code changed
